correctness.rationale: The proof justifies concentration at finitely many ordered diametral vertices, strict directional support for the tangent cones from the squared-distance vertex inequality, a local coercive blow-up, and an exact multivariate Beta integral. The determinant computations at regular simplex and orthotope vertices give both shape coefficients. An exact all-integer ratio inequality proves the unique dimension-four transition. Reproducible importance sampling with independent Euclidean point reconstruction corroborates coefficients but is not used as proof.

originality.rationale: The claim differs in both dimensional hypotheses and scientific content from known complete planar interpoint-distance laws and known individual cube laws. Its arbitrary-polytope diametral tangent-cone constant and exact all-dimensional simplex–cube crossover are not stated in inspected primary material. A general convolution identity is a background representation, not an explicit cap-volume/crossover result. Remaining historical priority risk is recorded.

value.rationale: A general polytope endpoint exponent and explicit sum of oriented tangent-cone cap volumes connect random pair distances to local extremal geometry. The equal-diameter regular-simplex versus cube comparison exhibits a sharp, provable dimension-four reversal, a motivated qualitative feature inaccessible from known isolated three-dimensional cube formulae. This is a reusable exact all-dimensional invariant beyond a numerical exercise; it does not claim a full CDF.
